description: A checked answer about unemployment benefits for a U.S. state, covering Alabama, Arizona, Idaho, Indiana, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, and Utah. Give a state (a name or 2-letter code) and either a topic or the person's own question; the tool picks the topic from the question when none is given. For a state we do not cover yet, it names the federal page that finds that state's own unemployment office instead of guessing at a figure. It only reads a checked guide: it cannot file a claim, check a claim's status, or change anyone's benefits.

question.description: The person's own question, used to pick a topic when none is given.

state.description: A U.S. state, by name or 2-letter code, such as "Texas" or "TX".

topic.description: One of the 13 topics: "home" (An overview: how to apply and what it pays.), "eligibility" (Who qualifies for unemployment benefits.), "apply" (How to file an unemployment claim.), "amounts" (How much it pays each week.), "duration" (How many weeks benefits last.), "weekly-claims" (Requesting payment and work search each week.), "jobs" (The state's own job search and job bank.), "appeals" (Denials, appeals, and overpayments.), "taxes" (How unemployment benefits are taxed.), "disability" (Disability benefits (SSDI, SSI) and how they relate to unemployment.), "offices" (The agency's offices and phone numbers.), "contact" (Who to contact about a specific claim.), "faq" (Common questions that cross several topics.). Leave out to pick the topic from the question instead.
